heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

MAYOR OF PAYAKUMBUH

WEST SUMATRA PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAYAKUMBUH CITY
PROTECTION
translated_text:
PROTECTION

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the City of Payakumbuh.
2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Payakumbuh.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Payakumbuh.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the Government of the City of Payakumbuh.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) measures.
6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and Parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including children still in the womb'
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, mentally, spiritually or socially.
12. Female victim of violence is a woman who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victim of violence is a child who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
18. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims;
21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence;
22. Shelter house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
23. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
21. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
27. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The regulation of protection of women and children aims to:
a. serve as a guideline for the Regional Government in planning, policies and strategies for the protection of women and children.
b. protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate the rights of women and children.
c. prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
d. increase empowerment of women.
e. increase the role and value of local wisdom and the role of customs in the protection of women and children, and
f. increase the role of government and non-government institutions in efforts to protect women and children.

heading: Article 4
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part one

Rights of women

heading: Article 5
Part two
translated_text:
Part two

Rights of children

heading: Article 6
CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

RESPONSIBILITIES OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY, PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

heading: Part One
Article 8
Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. In order to carry out its responsibilities, the Local Government shall establish programs and activities for the protection of women and children with a Regional Action Plan as the basis for SKPD in implementing the protection of women and children in accordance with their duties and functions.
2. Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The responsibilities of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. Participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of women's and children's rights;
b. Provide information and/or report violations of women's and children's rights to the competent authorities; and
c. Monitor the law enforcement process for cases of violations of women's and children's rights.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama, cadiak pandai and bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of women's and children's rights.
3. The responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on laws and regulations and local wisdom values of the local community.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Parents/Guardians and/or Family

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Responsibilities for the Protection of Women.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

The family in efforts to protect women's rights is responsible for:
a. Protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. Providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs, and
c. Preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Responsibilities for the Protection of Children

heading: Article 12
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

PREVENTION

Part One

Local Government

heading: Article 13
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. In the context of preventing violations against women's rights, the community:
a. Monitors various conditions occurring in its environment that may lead to violations against women's rights;
b. Strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. Prevents unregistered marriages/siri marriages.
2. In the context of preventing violations against children's rights, the community:
a. Monitors various conditions occurring in the environment that lead to violations against children's rights;
b. Strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. Prevents the occurrence of marriage at child age.

heading: Part three
translated_text:
Part three

Parents, family and/or guardians

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. In the context of preventing violations against children's rights, parents or guardians:
a. Provide good examples to children in accordance with religious and customary teachings;
b. Supervise children in their activities inside or outside the home;
c. Provide opportunities for children to engage in dialogue and express their opinions democratically; and
d. Protect children from various acts of violation of children's rights in the household.
2. In the context of preventing violations against women's rights, the family:
a. Protects women from various violations of rights in the household; and
b. Encourages the formation of a harmonious, educative and democratic family.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part one

Implementation of Protection of Women

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

General

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

Protection of women is implemented by the Regional Government by involving the active role of families, ninik mamak, bundo kanduang, customary leaders, religious leaders, the community and community organizations in the field of Protection of Women.

Paragraph 2 Marriage

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

During the marriage bond or after divorce, a woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Health Sector

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

The Regional Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for women.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

Public service providers are required to provide special facilities for breastfeeding.

Paragraph 4 Employment Sector

heading: Article 20
Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. Female workers/laborers under the age of 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves if working between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are required to:
a. Provide nutritious food and beverages; and
b. Maintain decency and security while at the workplace.
4. Employers are required to provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

heading: Paragraph 5
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Education Sector Article 22 Women are guaranteed freedom to obtain education at every level of formal and non-formal education.

heading: Paragraph 6
translated_text:
Paragraph 6

Social Sector

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. The regional government implements empowerment of women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability through productive economic business activities.
2. Community organizations may carry out empowerment for women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: Part two
translated_text:
Part two

Implementation of Protection of Children

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Health Sector Article 24 In the implementation of Protection of Children in the Health Sector, the Regional Government must:
1. Provide free health services for children from poor families.
2. Implement optimal health efforts for children, so that every child obtains a good degree of health from the womb.
3. Encourage infants to receive Exclusive Breastfeeding from their mothers properly and naturally.
4. Motivate children to receive adequate nutrition.
5. Protect children from attempts to transplant their body organs to other parties.
6. Conduct screening on newborns.
7. Monitor the growth and development of toddlers and pre-school age children.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Education Sector

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

Children in formal and non-formal educational institutions must be protected from acts of violence.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

The Regional Government and the community implement Early Childhood Education (PAUD).

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

For children aged 7 (seven) to 18 (eighteen) years who have not completed formal education/dropped out of school may pursue education through non-formal education units, namely:
a. Learning Group Package A equivalent to Elementary School and Madrasah Ibtidaiyah.
b. Learning Group Package B equivalent to Junior High School and Madrasah Tsanawiyah.
c. Learning Group Package C equivalent to Senior High School and Madrasah Aliyah and Vocational High School.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. Children with special needs and/or who have potential intelligence and/or special talents are given equal opportunities and facilities to obtain regular education or inclusive education.
2. Inclusive education as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regional Government and the community.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

Every organizer of formal education is prohibited from expelling children without guaranteeing the continuity of the child's education.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. The Regional Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for children from poor families, neglected children.
2. The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by the participation of the community and community organizations.
3. The implementation of the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: Article 31
Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Employment Sector

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. Employers are prohibited from employing children.
2. Employers are prohibited from forcing the use of religious attributes that are not in accordance with the religion adhered to by the worker.

heading: Article 33
Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

In the event that a company employs children as referred to in Article 33, the workplace for children must be separated from the workplace for adult workers.

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

Children may perform work in the workplace that is part of an educational or training curriculum approved by the authorized official.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. Everyone is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.
2. The worst forms of work as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. All work in the form of slavery or similar practices.
b. All work that exploits, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances or gambling.
c. All work that exploits, provides, or involves children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances and/or
d. All work that endangers the health, safety and morals of children.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social Sector

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide care for neglected children.
2. The care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social sector.
3. In the event that a child is neglected because for some reason the parents neglect, the Regional Government, Community Organizations as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the Court to determine the child as a neglected child.
4. The Court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) simultaneously determines the shelter and care for the neglected child concerned.

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. The Regional Government organizes skills training for street children and neglected children.
2. Skills training as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized by SKPD in accordance with their respective duties and functions.

heading: Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. The Regional Government provides shelters to foster street children and social institutions for neglected children.
2. Shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) may be organized in cooperation with community organizations.
3. Further provisions regarding shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

The implementation of protection for women and children is carried out by cross-sectoral SKPD whose duties and functions are related to the protection of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

HANDLING AND SERVICES

Part One

Handling of Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, family, community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. Directly.
b. By telephone; and
c. By letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 43, are also authorized to handle victims of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

The implementation of handling women and children victims of violence includes:
a. Handling complaints of victims of violence.
b. Health services
c. Social rehabilitation
d. Law enforcement and legal assistance, and
e. Repatriation and social reintegration.

heading: Article 43
Article 44
translated_text:
Article 44

Complaint handling services for victims of violence against women and children are carried out by:
a. Hospitals.
b. Community health centers.
c. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection (P2TP2A)
d. Women and Children Service Unit (UPPA)
e. Trauma Center Shelter (RPTC)
f. Child Social Shelter (RPSA)
g. Women Crisis Centre (WCC)
h. Marriage Counseling, Guidance and Preservation Agency (BP4)
i. Police
j. Prosecutor's Office
k. Legal Aid Institute (LBH) and
l. Child Protection Institute.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Health Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

heading: Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

1. Health services for women and children victims of violence include efforts covering promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
2. Health services for women and children victims of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, quality and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Special health services for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
4. Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. Medical services
b. Medicolegal services
c. Psychosocial counseling.
5. Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (4) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Article 46
translated_text:
Article 46

1. Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence are aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social Rehabilitation Services as referred to in paragraph (1) include counseling services, provision of safe houses and spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social sector.
b. SKPD that oversees women's empowerment and child protection.
c. Handling service institutions.

heading: Article 47
Article 48
translated_text:
Article 48

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and child victims of violence.
2. Safe houses aim to protect women and child victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women and child victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. Their life is threatened;
b. Receiving rejection from family or community;
c. Requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. Abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of:
a. Social workers;
b. Volunteers;
c. Security officers and
d. Community leaders
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

1. Women and child victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. Not imposing any religion and belief; and
b. Leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination)
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Advisory, Development and Preservation of Marriage Agency (BP4), Officers of the Religious Affairs Office (KUA), Ustads/Ulamas, Priests, Pastors and other gender-responsive religious leaders'

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Law Enforcement and Legal Aid Services

heading: Article 50
translated_text:
Article 50

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services are actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

heading: Article 5 1
translated_text:
Article 5 1

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services are intended to provide assistance and protection to women and child victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.
2. Types of legal aid services include:
a. Legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of BAP.
b. Legal aid in the prosecution process at the Prosecutor's Office.
c. Legal aid in the examination process at the Court.
d. Legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. Legal aid in the Mediation process.
f. Legal aid in the Diversion process.
3. The Regional Government provides legal aid to children and women victims of violence.
4. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with Legal Aid Institutions (LBH), Women Crisis Centres (WCC), Advocates and/or other gender-responsive legal assistants.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services

heading: Article 52
translated_text:
Article 52

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return women and child victims of violence to their area of origin;
2. Repatriation of women and child victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regional Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and child victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 53

1. The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for women.
2. The implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by the participation of the community and community organizations.

heading: Article 54
translated_text:
Article 54

1. The Regional Government provides skills training to increase women's capacity.
2. In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.
3. The Regional Government expands access and opportunities for women in obtaining employment opportunities.

heading: Article 55
translated_text:
Article 55

1. The Regional Government facilitates:
a. Provision of business capital for economically disadvantaged women.
b. Marketing of products resulting from women's businesses.
c. Organization of training for community capacity development through economic empowerment of pre-prosperous families.
d. Expansion of access, information and providing knowledge to women regarding marketing efforts for products produced; and
e. Providing comprehensive entrepreneurship training to women.
2. The Regional Government in facilitating activities as referred to in paragraph (1) cooperates with the community and/or community organizations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 56

1. Every child has ideas and the right to participate in conveying opinions, ideas, and others as well as being involved in decision-making processes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which are implemented with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
2. Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through children's forums starting from the Village, Sub-district and City levels.
3. Children's forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent children, both geographical domicile representation, socio-cultural groups and children's educational backgrounds.
4. The establishment of Children's Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) is facilitated by the Regional Government.
5. The establishment of children's forums as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

heading: Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

1. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government pays attention to and accommodates children's opinions conveyed through children's forums.
2. The Regional Government includes representatives of children's forums in Regional Development Deliberations.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CHILD-FRIENDLY CITY

Article 58

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance in the development of CFC (2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. Coordination.
b. Facilitation.
c. Guidance.
d. Education and training.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 59

1. Guidance for the implementation of protection of women and children is carried out by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (i) may be carried out in the form of;
a. Providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence.
b. Providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children.
c. Providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at Community Health Centers, integrated service units and General Hospitals.
d. Providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence, and
e. Improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.

heading: Article 60
translated_text:
Article 60

The Head of SKPD as a member of the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group (Pokja PUG) in accordance with their duties and functions is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of the protection program for women and children to the Mayor.

heading: Article 61
translated_text:
Article 61

1. The Mayor conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of protection of women and children on a regular basis.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) the Mayor may appoint SKPD in accordance with their duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for policies, programs for the protection of women and children in the region.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

FINANCING

Article 62

Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children is sourced from:
a Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 63

1. Any person or entity that violates Article 20, Article 21, Article 32, Article 33 and Article 36 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. A fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah);
b. Revocation of business license.
2. The procedure for the implementation of administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 64

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 65
translated_text:
Article 65

This Regional Regulation shall come into force from the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Payakumbuh City.

Stipulated in Payakumbuh on the date of

MAYOR OF PAYAKUMBUH,

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAYAKUMBUH CITY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAYAKUMBUH CITY

NUMBER 1 YEAR 2016 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAYAKUMBUH CITY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty which we must always protect because in them is inherent dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves according to their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, laws and regulations that can guarantee its implementation.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (Child Right Convention) affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from abduction, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of the Child, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, especially in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children.

heading: Article 43

translated_text:
Article 43

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Point b What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services to victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in the provision of services. Officers must convey this principle to victims Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background and life experience so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any way.

Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken. Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language that is understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Lately there are more and more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind or mentally retarded. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example, who can be taken from special school teachers.

Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. Perhaps several interventions require various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.

Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.

Point l What is meant by the fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the convention on the rights of the children. Convention on the elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women (convention on the elimination of All Against Women)
